# @ic-reactor/react — AI Quick Guide

Use this file when your app installs `@ic-reactor/react` and you need fast,
accurate integration guidance.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/react @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/react-query
pnpm add @icp-sdk/auth@^10 # optional auth helpers; v10 recommended, v8 also supported
```

`@icp-sdk/auth` v10 is the first release that peers `@icp-sdk/core@^6`, which
this package needs, so npm installs the set as published. v8 still works, but
every v8 release peers `@icp-sdk/core@^5`, so on npm it needs
`{"overrides":{"@icp-sdk/auth":{"@icp-sdk/core":"$@icp-sdk/core"}}}` in
`package.json`. pnpm and yarn do not. v7 and v9 are not supported.

## Start Here

- Fastest setup: `defineReactor(...)` (raw Candid values) or
  `defineDisplayReactor(...)` (display values); same options
- Server-rendered app (Next.js, any React SSR): `createReactorProvider(factory)`
- Existing reactor instance: `createActorHooks(reactor)`
- Reusable shared operations: `createQuery(...)`, `createMutation(...)`

## Inside React vs Outside React (critical)

- Inside React components/custom hooks: `useActorQuery`, `useActorMutation`,
  `useActorMethod`, `.useQuery()`, `.useMutation()`
- Outside React (loaders/actions/services/tests): `.fetch()`, `.prefetch()`,
  `.invalidate()`, `.getCacheData()`, `.execute(args)`
- A sign-in or sign-out while `.fetch()` is in flight makes it fetch again for
  the new identity; it does not reject with TanStack's `CancelledError`

Never call React hooks in loaders, actions, route modules, scripts, or tests.

A React Server Component, server action or route handler may import
`Reactor`, `DisplayReactor`, `ClientManager` and the rest of the core runtime
from `@ic-reactor/react`: Next.js resolves the package's `react-server` export
condition to an entry without hooks. Build them inside the request, never at
module scope, and call `reactor.fetchQuery()` / `reactor.callMethod()` there.
Hooks, `defineReactor`, `createActorHooks`, `createReactorProvider`, the
query/mutation factories and the auth classes are missing exports in that
graph; they belong in a `"use client"` module.

## Server-Rendered Apps: createReactorProvider

A module-scope reactor on a server is one cache shared by every request (query
keys carry no caller). Build client-side reactors per mount instead:

```tsx
"use client"
import { createReactorProvider, defineReactor } from "@ic-reactor/react"

export const { ReactorProvider, useReactor } = createReactorProvider(() =>
  defineReactor<_SERVICE>({ name: "backend", idlFactory, canisterId })
)

// layout: <ReactorProvider>{children}</ReactorProvider>
// component: const { useActorQuery, useAuth } = useReactor()
```

- The factory runs once per mounted provider (once per request on a server);
  it may return a record (`useReactor("ledger")`) or query/mutation objects.
- `useReactor()` is typed as the factory's return: never write `as any` hook
  forwarders or a hand-rolled context + `useEffect(dispose)` provider.
- It disposes the `AuthenticationManager`s built for the value (in the factory,
  or later by a `defineReactor` result in it) on unmount, leaves managers built
  elsewhere alone, and renders a `QueryClientProvider` for the value's single
  QueryClient.
- Factory props are read once per mount; change the provider's `key` to rebuild.
- A provider mounted by a transition (router navigation, `startTransition`)
  needs a `<Suspense>` boundary inside it around components that use suspense
  hooks; otherwise each retry can rebuild the value and refetch.
- Never call `createAuthHooks`/`createActorHooks` during render; take the hooks
  from `useReactor()`.

## Display vs Raw Values

- Prefer `defineDisplayReactor(...)` (or `DisplayReactor`) for UI/form code.
  `defineReactor({ display: true })` is deprecated; do not generate it.
- Use raw `Reactor` when you intentionally need native `bigint`/`Principal`.
- Token amounts are base units (e8s) either way. Show one with
  `formatTokenAmount(balance, decimals, { maxFractionDigits: 4 })` and read
  typed text with `parseTokenAmount(text, decimals)` (a `bigint`; pass
  `.toString()` to a `DisplayReactor`). Never `Number(x) / 10 ** decimals` or
  `Math.floor(Number(text) * 10 ** decimals)`: both lose digits. Both helpers
  are also exported from the `react-server` entry.
- Bundle cost: `DisplayReactor` adds zod (about 24 kB gzipped). Until the next
  major, `defineReactor` includes it too, because of the deprecated flag; the
  smallest setup is `createActorHooks(new Reactor(...))` + `createAuthHooks`.

## Queries Whose Args Are Not Known Yet

Pass `skipToken` (re-exported from TanStack Query) in place of args; the
query waits without calling the canister and fetches once the args exist:

```ts
import { skipToken } from "@ic-reactor/react"

const { data } = useActorQuery({
  functionName: "icrc1_balance_of",
  args: owner ? [{ owner, subaccount: [] }] : skipToken,
})

// A factory from createQueryFactory: its skipped query has only useQuery()
const getBalance = createQueryFactory(ledger, { functionName: "icrc1_balance_of" })
const { data: same } = getBalance(
  owner ? [{ owner, subaccount: [] }] : skipToken
).useQuery()
```

It works in `useActorQuery`, `useReactorQuery`, `useActorInfiniteQuery`
(`getArgs: skipToken`) and query factories from `createQueryFactory`. Never
write `args: [owner!]`, a placeholder account or `as any` plus `enabled`. The
suspense hooks and factories reject it; keep `enabled` for conditions that are
not about missing args.

## Many Canisters of One Interface

For a multi-token wallet, make one reactor and derive the others with
`reactor.forCanister(canisterId)`: a memoized sibling of the same class on the
same `ClientManager`, keyed by its own canister. Build hooks on it with
`useMemo(() => createActorHooks(ledger.forCanister(id)), [id])`. A single query
object can instead take `callConfig: { canisterId }` in `createQuery`,
`createSuspenseQuery` and their factories. Do not retarget a shared reactor
with `setCanisterId`, or add the canister to `queryKey` by hand: keys already
start with the canister.

## Types From a Reactor

To type a prop, form state or error view, read the type off the reactor:
`ReactorArgsOf<typeof reactor, "method">[0]`, `ReactorDataOf<typeof reactor,
"method">` and `ReactorErrorOf<typeof reactor, "method">` (re-exported from
core). They follow the reactor's transform, so do not hand-write display
shapes or spell out `ReactorReturnErr<_SERVICE, M, "display">`.

## Update Methods: Use Mutations

Query hooks and factories run their method again on every refetch (mount,
window focus, reconnect, invalidation) and retry, and an update method
executes on the canister each time. Use `useActorMutation`, `useActorMethod`
or `createMutation` for methods that change state; pass an update method to a
query only when repeating it is safe (a certified read).

Without a `retry` of its own, a query of an update method retries only a
`SysTransient` rejection (`isRetryableUpdateError`), within the QueryClient's
`retry` default. Mutations retry nothing unless `retry` is set on them or as
the QueryClient's `mutations.retry` default, which also reaches
`useActorMethod` update calls and `createMutation().execute()`; use
`reactorUpdateRetry` to retry a mutation only when that cannot run it twice.

## Invalidating After a Mutation

`invalidateQueries` on `createMutation`, `.useMutation()`, `useActorMutation`
and `useActorMethod` takes, per entry: a `{ functionName, args? }` method of
the mutation's reactor (type-checked; without `args` it covers every query of
the method, infinite ones included), a query object, a query factory (every
query it returns, whatever the args), or a query key. The invalidation is
awaited before `onSuccess`. Never hand-write a key such as `["get_posts"]`:
keys start with the canister ID, so it matches nothing.

```ts
const createPost = createMutation(backend, {
  functionName: "create_post",
  invalidateQueries: [getPosts, { functionName: "get_posts_count" }],
})
```

A query factory function also has `getQueryKey()` (the prefix of all its
queries) and `invalidate()`.

## Optimistic Updates

Use the query object's `optimisticUpdate(updater)`, never a hand-rolled
cancel/snapshot/`setQueryData`/rollback or `useQueryClient()` (it throws
without the optional `QueryClientProvider`; use `reactor.queryClient`):

```ts
const getPost = createQueryFactory(backend, { functionName: "get_post" })
const likePost = createMutation(backend, { functionName: "like_post" })

// In a component
const { mutate } = likePost.useMutation({
  onMutate: ([postId]) =>
    getPost([postId]).optimisticUpdate((post) => ({
      ...post,
      likes: post.likes + 1n,
    })),
  onError: (_error, _args, update) => update?.rollback(),
  onSettled: (_data, _error, [postId]) => getPost([postId]).invalidate(),
})
```

The updater gets the typed raw (pre-`select`) value and is skipped when
nothing is cached. Always refetch once the mutation settles (`onSettled`
`invalidate()`, or the query in `invalidateQueries`): the fetch it cancels may
be a refetch an invalidation or a sign-in started. `rollback()` does nothing
after a sign-in or sign-out, since the snapshot was the previous principal's.
Query objects also have `cancel()` and `reset()` (reset re-suspends a suspense
query). All three act on the query's own entry only.

## Mutation Error Handling

For canister `Result.Err` variants, use `onCanisterError`. Keep `onError` for
network/agent and unexpected errors.

## Testing

- Import `installFakeReplica` and `createTestCanister` from
  `@ic-reactor/react/testing` (the same as `@ic-reactor/core/testing`) and run
  the real reactor and hooks against the fake replica, instead of a stub cast
  `as unknown as Reactor`.
- Install the fake before any `ClientManager` is built, and point it at
  `replica.host`. For a module-scope `defineReactor(...)`, install the fake at
  the top of the test file (or in a Vitest setup file) and `await import(...)`
  the component afterwards; in Vitest's jsdom a manager with no `host` uses the
  page origin, `http://localhost:3000`, so pass that as the fake's `host`.
- Reset a shared reactor between tests with `queryClient.clear()`.
- Test a signed-in user with `clientManager.updateAgent(identity)`; the kit does
  not simulate Internet Identity sign-in.

## Generated Files

Do not hand-edit generated `index.generated.ts` files. Put app-specific code in
`index.ts` wrappers or separate factory modules.
